method: Seven fresh frozen shots; each paired with its canonical official reference using randomized A/B order. Quality winner was chosen before opening the mapping key.

results.gap: Stamped low-poly foliage, flat shoulder planes, and weaker near/mid/far terrain depth.
Warm-light reference has natural material response and continuous terrain; ours remains faceted and washed in comparison.
Night reference has readable headlights, road reflections, and mountain silhouettes; ours is very dark with flat low-poly verge detail.
Cockpit reference has detailed physical dashboard and believable road/guardrail integration; ours has a stylized low-poly interior and terrain.
Reference keeps soft overcast material contrast and realistic roadside slope; ours has coarse autumn cards and hard ground planes.
Correct terrestrial winter fixture is present, but reference snow terrain is layered and naturally blended while ours is a flat white shoulder with sparse cards.
Reference has coherent lake/landform scale and atmospheric layers; ours reads as a high polygon road slab over a shallow field.

summary.largest_gap: Continuous grounded landscape depth and material integration: repeated billboard/card vegetation and broad hard-edged shoulder planes remain visibly procedural versus the reference's smooth, layered landform, foliage, and contact shading.
summary.road_terrain_note: No visible road/terrain z-fighting or mesh penetration in the seven frozen views. The road edge is clean, but an abrupt shoulder/material seam remains and should not be treated as fully blended contact.
